title: Nabu common definitions
$comment: v0 (Phase 0). Identifier types shared by every other schema. Regexes are written in the common subset of ECMA-262, Python re and Rust regex so all validators agree.

LangTag.title: LangTag
LangTag.description: A well-formed BCP 47 language tag in canonical case (language lowercase, Script titlecase, REGION uppercase). Extlangs and grandfathered tags are not accepted; use their canonical replacements.

ScriptedLangTag.title: ScriptedLangTag
ScriptedLangTag.description: A LangTag that carries an explicit script subtag. Every piece of language data uses one (gameplan §1 decision 3, §6.1): direction, fonts, Han glyph selection and input all key off the script.

OrthographyId.title: OrthographyId
OrthographyId.description: Identifies an orthography profile: a ScriptedLangTag, a slash, and a lowercase slug.

SchemeId.title: SchemeId
SchemeId.description: A reading or annotation scheme, such as jyutping, pinyin, furigana or ipa.

SenseId.title: SenseId
SenseId.description: Links a token to a lexicon entry. An authored slug in NFC; may be in the target script. No whitespace.

KcId.title: KcId
KcId.description: A knowledge-component id: its kind (§7.1), a colon, and an authored slug.

Persons.title: Persons
Persons.description: Who says a sentence and who it is said to, where the target language marks it and the support language does not: a masculine or feminine you, a singular, dual or plural you, a speaker's gender on adjectives (Arabic jou3an / jou3ane). The prompt shows it when the learner writes the sentence in the target language, so the accept set holds only the forms that fit. A course should exercise every value its language marks, not one (ADR 0075).

speaker.description: The speaker's gender, where the sentence marks it.

addressee.description: Who is spoken to: one man (m), one woman (f), one person where the language marks number but not gender (sg: Cantonese 你 against 你哋), two people where it has a dual (du), or several people (pl).

Facet.title: Facet
Facet.description: What an exercise practises about a knowledge component (gameplan §8.5): recognizing it, producing it, hearing it, saying it, reading or writing its script.

PlacementPolicy.title: PlacementPolicy
PlacementPolicy.description: How a course's placement test probes (ADR 0077). By default it checks production with word tiles, which is quick; `typed` has the learner type, which also checks spelling and accent marks: what a heritage speaker most often lacks.

ScriptCode.title: ScriptCode
ScriptCode.description: An ISO 15924 script code in titlecase.

Names.title: Names
Names.description: A name in the languages it is given in (BCP 47 tags; ADR 0109): data, not app messages. The app shows the one in the UI language, else the first.

CourseNames.title: CourseNames
CourseNames.description: What the app calls a course and the orthographies it teaches, and the lines the course list says of them, by the language they are written in (a BCP 47 tag; ADR 0109). Course data, never app messages: a new course needs no catalog entry. The app shows them in the UI language where the course gives them.

course.description: The course's name, as other text names it: Cantonese, Lebanese Arabic, Biblical Hebrew.

blurb.description: One line on what the course teaches, under its name in the course list: The Arabic of Lebanon, as people speak it every day.

orthographies.description: Each orthography's name, where the course teaches more than one or the name says more than the script's: Arabizi (Latin letters and numbers).

hints.description: For a course in several orthographies, what choosing each means, under its name in the course list: Latin letters and digits, as many Lebanese write in messages.
